The common thread across all three: every output is traceable, every analytical decision is logged, and every recommendation is designed to be reviewed and validated by the scientific team before it drives a decision. title: 5 AI Tools for Janitorial Lead Generation
summary: Explore five AI tools that streamline lead generation for janitorial businesses, enhancing client engagement and boosting efficiency.
body_text: Finding new clients for your janitorial business doesn’t have to be a time-consuming process anymore. AI tools are now simplifying lead generation, allowing cleaning companies to identify, engage, and convert potential customers faster and more efficiently. These tools help you target local businesses, send personalized emails, and even automate entire outreach campaigns. Here are five AI-powered tools tailored for janitorial lead generation : Cohesive AI : Automates lead generation by scraping data from sources like Google Maps, creating targeted lists, and managing email campaigns. It also personalizes outreach to increase response rates. Cost: $500/month + $75 setup fee. Convex : Focuses on property intelligence and buyer intent to identify high-value leads. Pricing is custom and suited for businesses pursuing larger contracts. AI Voice Receptionists & Chatbots : Handle inquiries 24/7, provide instant quotes , and qualify leads via website chats, calls, or social media. Pricing starts at $40–$100/month. CRM Systems with AI Lead Nurturing : Automate follow-ups, segment leads, and manage sales pipelines. Costs range from $15–$50 per user/month. AI Quote Forms & Lead Capture Tools : Turn website visitors into leads by qualifying them in real time and providing instant quotes. Pricing starts at $20–$50/month. These tools streamline the entire sales process, from finding leads to closing deals. Whether you’re a small business or targeting larger contracts, there’s an AI tool to fit your needs. Quick Comparison Tool Key Features Pricing Best Use Cases Cohesive AI Local targeting , email campaigns, CRM integration $500/month + $75 setup Automating lead generation for local markets Convex Property insights, buyer intent analysis Custom pricing High-value commercial contracts AI Voice Receptionists & Chatbots 24/7 lead handling, instant quotes $40–$100/month After-hours inquiries and website engagement CRM Systems with AI Lead nurturing, follow-ups, segmentation $15–$50/user/month Managing and converting captured leads AI Quote Forms Real-time qualification, instant quotes $20–$50/month Website-based lead generation These tools offer janitorial businesses a way to grow their client base without relying on outdated methods like cold calling or generic emails. By automating and personalizing outreach, you can focus on delivering quality services while AI handles the rest. How to Find UNLIMITED Commercial Cleaning Leads Using Google Maps + AI (Decision Makers) 1. Cohesive AI Cohesive AI is a specialized lead generation platform tailored for local service businesses, particularly janitorial companies. By automating the process of identifying and connecting with potential clients, it offers a streamlined solution for cleaning businesses aiming to grow without the hassle of manual prospecting. Lead Generation Capabilities The platform's standout feature is its ability to gather data from multiple sources to create highly targeted prospect lists. Since janitorial companies typically operate within specific areas, Cohesive AI focuses on local business targeting . It pulls information from sources like Google Maps and government filings to pinpoint local business owners who are likely decision-makers for cleaning contracts. This approach minimizes irrelevant or outdated contacts, saving time and effort. What sets Cohesive AI apart is its data filtering process , which ensures only businesses matching the ideal customer profile are included. This means janitorial companies can spend less time chasing unqualified leads and more time engaging with businesses that genuinely need their services. This precise data collection forms the backbone of its automation features, making lead generation more efficient. Automation Features Cohesive AI operates on a fully automated model , managing the entire lead generation process from start to finish. It handles tasks like data extraction, building prospect lists, creating personalized emails, managing campaigns, and even follow-up sequences - freeing up time for business owners to focus on other priorities. One of its key advantages is the ability to run three campaigns simultaneously , allowing janitorial companies to target multiple markets or service areas at once. For instance, a business could simultaneously reach out to office buildings, medical facilities, and retail spaces, tailoring each campaign to its audience. The platform also includes email deliverability management , ensuring emails are sent successfully while maintaining domain reputation and complying with anti-spam regulations. Personalization Options Cohesive AI takes automation a step further with its personalized messaging capabilities. Its AI-driven system analyzes public data about target businesses to craft tailored emails. Instead of sending generic messages like "we offer cleaning services", it creates emails that address specific challenges or needs relevant to each prospect's industry or business type. This personalized approach is a game-changer for engagement. Studies show that personalized email campaigns can boost response rates by up to 50% [1] . For janitorial companies, this translates to more meaningful interactions and better-qualified leads entering their sales funnels. With Cohesive AI, the time-consuming task of crafting individualized messages happens automatically, giving businesses a competitive edge without extra effort. Integration with Sales/CRM Systems Cohesive AI doesn't just stop at generating leads - it integrates seamlessly with existing workflows. While it includes its own built-in CRM and marketing tools , it also allows businesses to export leads and campaign data in formats compatible with popular CRM platforms. This means janitorial companies can effortlessly transfer qualified leads into their current systems without disrupting their established processes. This flexibility ensures that businesses can adopt Cohesive AI without retraining their teams or overhauling their workflows. Instead, it enhances what’s already in place by feeding high-quality leads directly into their sales pipelines. The platform is priced at $500 per month with a one-time $75 onboarding fee . There are no long-term contracts, and it comes with a performance guarantee: at least four interested responses per month, or the company provides a free month of service. This guarantee makes it a low-risk option for janitorial businesses exploring AI-driven lead generation for the first time. 2. Convex There's currently no verified data available on how well Convex performs in terms of lead generation, automation features, or CRM integrations specifically for janitorial businesses. This lack of information underscores the difficulty of assessing newer AI tools in a fast-changing market. Including Convex here, despite the limited data, provides a broader view of the tools currently available in the AI space. As the industry progresses, more reliable details about Convex may become available, shedding light on its potential for janitorial lead generation. 3. AI Voice Receptionists and Chatbots AI voice receptionists and chatbots work tirelessly to capture leads 24/7. These systems manage incoming calls, website chats, and social media messages, ensuring potential customers get immediate responses. They pair seamlessly with automated email campaigns and data-driven targeting strategies, making them an essential part of a modern lead-generation toolkit. Take Ochatbot 's LeadBot , for example. Specifically designed for cleaning services, it boasts an incredibly quick setup - ready to go in under 30 seconds - and integrates effortlessly with existing business websites [7] . Similarly, Voiceflow offers AI-powered chatbots tailored for cleaning companies, providing instant quotes and earning an impressive 4.7/5 user rating [3] . Lead Generation Capabilities These tools excel at capturing leads across multiple channels, including phone calls, web chats, SMS messages, and social media. This omnichannel approach ensures no potential customer is overlooked. By engaging prospects on their preferred platforms, businesses can significantly boost conversion rates and reduce the number of missed opportunities [3] . Automation Features AI-driven automation takes lead qualification to the next level. Chatbots can instantly provide quotes, answer common questions, and even schedule appointments - all without human involvement [3] . Voice AI agents further enhance efficiency by routing qualified leads directly into sales pipelines, sending follow-up emails or SMS messages, and syncing appointments with calendars. These features integrate smoothly into broader sales workflows, saving time and maximizing productivity. Personalization Options Beyond basic automation, advanced AI systems personalize interactions by adapting conversation flows based on user responses. They can recall previous interactions to offer better recommendations [7] and tailor responses based on a customer’s location or specific needs, which can dramatically improve conversion rates [3] [2] . Many platforms also support multiple languages, a critical feature in the diverse markets of the United States [7] . Integration with Sales/CRM Systems These tools integrate seamlessly with CRM systems, ensuring that qualified lead data flows directly into existing sales pipelines. Notifications for sales teams and synchronized appointment bookings keep everything running smoothly [7] . This streamlined approach not only improves the handoff from lead capture to follow-up but also helps businesses maintain consistent branding and tone [3] [2] . Pricing for these solutions typically starts at $49–$99 per month for basic features like lead capture and quoting. More advanced options, including voice AI agents and deeper integrations, may cost more depending on usage [3] [2] . While these systems handle routine interactions effectively, they may need regular monitoring and occasional tweaks to manage more complex customer inquiries. 4. CRM Systems with AI Lead Nurturing Once AI chatbots capture leads, the next step is nurturing and converting them into customers. This is where AI-powered CRM systems shine. These tools simplify the sales process for janitorial businesses by automating lead nurturing - from the first interaction to the final contract. They do much more than just store contact information; they identify high-potential leads, automate follow-ups, and tailor outreach efforts on a large scale. Lead Generation Capabilities AI-driven CRM platforms excel at analyzing data from sources like property records, permit filings, and online activity. By doing so, they qualify and segment leads based on factors like facility size, industry, and location. This targeted approach can significantly shorten sales cycles - from the usual 4–6 weeks to just 2–3 weeks [8] [6] . These systems also use algorithms to score leads based on their intent and past interactions, helping sales teams zero in on the most promising prospects [8] . Automation Features One standout feature of AI CRM systems is their ability to automate time-consuming tasks. They instantly route qualified leads to the right sales reps and handle follow-up sequences using personalized emails and automated notifications - all without manual input [8] . Since sales reps often spend up to 72% of their time on non-sales activities, this level of automation frees them to focus on what they do best: closing deals [8] . The result is a more tailored and efficient approach to engaging leads. Personalization Options Personalization is another area where AI CRM platforms excel. By leveraging enriched data and machine learning, these systems craft messages that feel uniquely tailored to each lead. For instance, they can reference details like facility size, recent permit filings, or even current service providers. Generative AI takes this a step further by creating customized sales proposals that resonate with decision-makers, increasing the chances of engagement and conversion. Integration with Sales and Marketing Tools AI CRM systems also play well with other tools in your tech stack. They integrate seamlessly with platforms like email marketing services, property intelligence tools, and scheduling software. Popular options such as Apollo and LinkedIn are often included, making workflows smoother and improving targeting accuracy [4] . Janitorial businesses that adopt these systems frequently report conversion rate boosts of 20–30%. Additionally, built-in compliance features ensure adherence to regulations like the CAN-SPAM Act and CCPA [8] . For small to mid-sized janitorial businesses, pricing typically falls between $50 and $300 per user per month. Many platforms also offer free trials or demos, making it easier to test their features before committing [4] . 5. AI Quote Forms and Lead Capture Tools AI quote forms turn your website into a round-the-clock lead generation powerhouse. Unlike basic contact forms that only gather surface-level details, these advanced tools engage visitors in meaningful conversations, qualify prospects in real time, and deliver customized quotes instantly. By building on earlier advancements in AI, they offer speed and precision when it comes to capturing potential clients. Lead Generation Capabilities AI quote forms don’t just collect information - they actively convert visitors into qualified leads. They ask targeted questions about things like service type, square footage, cleaning frequency, and budget. And because they operate 24/7, they’re perfect for industries like janitorial services, where facility managers often work odd hours. For example, a commercial property manager looking for cleaning services on a late Sunday night can receive an instant quote and schedule a callback for the next business day. These tools go beyond the basics by gathering detailed information such as specific cleaning needs, current service providers, and decision-making timelines. This ensures your sales team is armed with all the details they need to close deals faster and more effectively. Automation Features Modern AI lead capture tools can handle up to 80% of routine inquiries [5] , freeing up your team to focus on more strategic tasks. These systems can schedule appointments, send follow-up emails, and even create preliminary service proposals based on the information prospects provide. Take, for instance, a mid-sized commercial cleaning company in Dallas that implemented Voiceflow's AI-powered quote form in July 2024. Within three months, they saw a 28% jump in qualified leads and cut their average response time from 12 hours to under 1 hour [3] . The tool automatically pre-qualified leads based on service type and square footage and even scheduled callbacks - completely eliminating the need for manual intervention. Personalization Options AI-powered quote forms deliver a personalized experience that feels like a one-on-one conversation. They adapt dynamically to user responses, mimicking the flow of a real sales interaction. For example, if someone indicates they need post-construction cleanup, the system can immediately ask about debris types, timeline constraints, and any specialized equipment requirements. This personalization extends to the quotes themselves. Based on factors like square footage, cleaning frequency, and specific service needs, the system generates tailored pricing estimates. Add in local touches - like referencing nearby clients (with permission) or adjusting pricing to reflect regional market trends - and you’ve got a tool that not only engages prospects but also boosts conversion rates. Integration with Sales and CRM Systems These AI tools don’t just stop at capturing leads - they seamlessly integrate with popular CRM platforms like HubSpot , Salesforce , and Zoho . This means that once a prospect fills out a form - even in the middle of the night - their information is automatically added to your sales pipeline for tracking and follow-up. Post-capture processes like automated email campaigns, SMS reminders, and scheduled callbacks help nurture leads at every stage of their journey. On top of that, many platforms provide detailed analytics, tracking metrics like form performance, conversion rates by traffic source, and lead quality. This data allows janitorial businesses to continually refine their lead capture strategies and maximize their return on investment. Tool Comparison Chart This chart provides a quick overview of the key features, pricing, and ideal use cases for five AI tools designed to enhance janitorial lead generation. It condenses the detailed reviews above, making it easier to compare options at a glance. Tool Main Features Pricing (USD) Best Use Cases Cohesive AI Scrapes Google Maps and government filings, AI-personalized cold emails, fully managed email campaigns, CRM integration, supports up to 3 simultaneous campaigns $500/month + $75 setup fee Local janitorial businesses looking for full automation to replace traditional lead generation methods Convex Property intelligence, buyer intent analysis, automated follow-ups, personalized proposals, high-intent prospect identification Custom pricing (premium) Commercial janitorial services pursuing high-value contracts AI Voice Receptionists & Chatbots 24/7 lead capture, instant quotes, customer inquiry handling, real-time engagement $40–$100+/month Website lead capture and after-hours customer service CRM Systems with AI Lead Nurturing Automated follow-ups, lead segmentation, personalized communications, pipeline management $15–$50+/user/month Ongoing lead nurturing and managing sales pipelines AI Quote Forms & Lead Capture Tools Automated intake, lead qualification, real-time routing, 24/7 availability $20–$50+/month Simplified web-based lead generation and customer onboarding Budget Considerations for Small to Medium Businesses For janitorial companies new to AI tools, starting with AI Quote Forms or basic CRM systems can be a cost-effective choice, with prices beginning around $20 per month. These tools provide essential features without stretching the budget. On the other hand, businesses accustomed to investing heavily in lead generation may find Cohesive AI a worthwhile option. Its flat fee includes a guarantee of at least four interested responses per month - or a free month credit if that threshold isn’t met. Integration and Scalability Factors Tools like CRM systems and AI chatbots integrate seamlessly with existing websites and scheduling software, requiring minimal setup. However, more comprehensive platforms, such as Cohesive AI and Convex , may involve some workflow adjustments to make the most of their automation capabilities. ROI Timeline Expectations Platforms leveraging property intelligence, like Convex , can significantly shorten sales cycles - reducing a typical 4- to 6-week cycle to just 2–3 weeks by focusing on high-intent prospects [8] . Meanwhile, tools like AI chatbots and lead capture forms often deliver immediate results by increasing lead volume. For more integrated systems, expect a bit of a ramp-up period as campaigns fine-tune for optimal performance. These insights help set the stage for selecting the tool that aligns best with your business goals, ensuring a smooth transition to enhanced lead generation. Conclusion AI tools are transforming the way janitorial companies across the United States connect with potential customers. Gone are the days of relying solely on manual prospecting, cold calls, or costly lead generation agencies. Today, these businesses can use AI to automate the process of finding prospects, achieving better results while keeping costs in check. This shift not only simplifies customer acquisition but also allows companies to channel more energy into delivering quality cleaning services. With AI-driven lead nurturing, businesses can see up to a 50% increase in qualified leads at just one-third of the usual cost [1] . By moving from reactive to proactive strategies, janitorial companies can focus on what they do best - providing excellent cleaning solutions - while AI takes care of the heavy lifting with automation and personalized outreach. One of the most game-changing aspects of AI is its ability to level the playing field for smaller janitorial firms. A local cleaning business can now compete with larger enterprises by using advanced automation and personalization tools that were once only available to companies with hefty marketing budgets. Whether you’re starting with a basic AI tool or opting for a more robust platform like Cohesive AI - priced at $500 per month with a one-time $75 setup fee - there’s an option to suit your budget and growth strategy. These advancements allow janitorial companies to respond more quickly to inquiries, nurture leads more effectively, and expand their customer base without adding significantly to their workload. Early adopters of AI tools are better positioned to capture market share and meet the shifting expectations of today’s digital-savvy clients. For traditional janitorial businesses, embracing AI isn't just an option - it’s a necessary step to stay competitive and thrive in the evolving cleaning services industry. FAQs How can AI tools help small janitorial businesses generate leads more effectively than traditional methods? AI tools, such as Cohesive AI, offer small janitorial businesses a faster, more efficient way to find and connect with potential clients. Instead of spending hours on manual tasks, these tools can automate processes like pinpointing local businesses through Google Maps, gathering contact details, and crafting personalized cold emails. With capabilities like AI-powered email personalization and campaign management, businesses can roll out targeted outreach campaigns in as little as 24 hours. This approach not only cuts down on the need for expensive lead generation services but also delivers more accurate and effective results. What should janitorial businesses look for in an AI tool for lead generation? When choosing an AI tool for lead generation, janitorial businesses should focus on features that simplify tasks and maximize efficiency. Opt for tools that can automatically find local leads , customize cold emails , and effectively handle email campaigns . It's also crucial that the tool includes dependable email deliverability management and automates tasks like gathering local business data. These functions can significantly cut down on manual work and boost the effectiveness of your outreach efforts. How can AI-powered CRM tools improve lead nurturing for janitorial businesses? AI-driven CRM tools simplify lead nurturing by automating essential tasks such as outreach and follow-ups. For janitorial businesses, these tools can tailor communication, helping to connect with potential clients in a more personalized way and fostering trust. Take platforms like Cohesive AI, for instance. They can handle lead generation by pinpointing local business owners, creating customized cold emails, and running email campaigns. This frees up time for janitorial companies to concentrate on scheduling cleaning walkthroughs and providing top-notch services, all while reducing the workload. title: Deal Insights Dashboard: What Sales Leaders Actually Use (vs What They Ignore)
summary: Sales leaders check three things on a deal insights dashboard and ignore the rest. Here's what actually gets used — and why most dashboards go unread.
body_text: Sales leaders check three things on a deal insights dashboard: at-risk deals this quarter, rep-level activity against target, and forecast accuracy. Everything else — call sentiment scores, talk-to-listen ratios, competitor mention frequency, keyword trends — gets built, shipped, and ignored. 67.7% of business leaders say they use dashboards to monitor sales performance , up from 54% in 2023. But only 34% of organizations are highly confident in their deal insights . The gap between “we have a dashboard” and “it changes what we do” is where most sales tech budget disappears. This post breaks down what gets used, what gets ignored, and why the next generation of deal insights is moving from dashboards to actions taken on behalf of the rep. The three things sales leaders check Ask any VP Sales what they open on Monday morning and you'll get a version of the same list. 1. At-risk deals in the current quarter. Not every deal at risk — just the ones big enough to move the number. A VP running a EUR 4M quarter cares about the six-figure deals slipping, not the EUR 8k SMB that went quiet. Which named deals moved backwards this week, and why. 2. Rep-level activity against target. Meetings booked, calls made, pipeline created, pipeline closed. This is the coaching-and-accountability layer. It answers the question the VP has to answer to their CRO: is this a team problem or a person problem? 3. Forecast accuracy over time. Not this quarter's forecast — the delta between what reps committed 30 days ago and what closed. This is the trust metric. It tells the leader whether their pipeline conversations are reality-based or wishful. Three things. Everything else on the dashboard is either input to one of these three, or it's noise the leader has trained themselves to scroll past. What gets built and ignored Modern conversation intelligence platforms ship dashboards with 20 to 40 widgets. Here's what sales leaders skip: Talk-to-listen ratios. Interesting once. Actionable never. A leader isn't going to open a dashboard, see rep X talked 62% of the time, and do anything about it during business hours. Sentiment scores. “This call had negative sentiment” is not a next action. The rep already knew. Keyword and competitor mention trends. Useful for marketing and product. Not for a sales leader trying to hit a number this quarter. Call volume heat maps. Pretty. Uncorrelated with revenue. Team-wide “top objections this month” clouds. Good for a QBR slide. Never checked between QBRs. Custom-property fill rates. Dataparrot's own product update leads with fill-rate analytics as a feature. Sales leaders care about fill rates when their CRM is on fire — which is most of the time, but the dashboard doesn't fix it. The pattern is clear. Sales leaders ignore anything that doesn't map to a named deal or a named rep, and anything that doesn't tell them what to do next. They don't need more visibility. They need fewer, sharper decisions surfaced at the moment they can act on them. Why “more metrics” is the wrong direction The default take in the category is that a better dashboard has more data. FreJun's 2025 sales statistics roundup points out that 35–50% of deals go to the vendor who responds first, and 45–50% of B2B deals need 5–8 follow-ups. The insight isn't hidden. The problem isn't visibility. Watching a dashboard doesn't respond, follow up, or update the CRM. A rep does. Or an AI agent does. This is where conversation intelligence stops short. It records the call, transcribes it, flags the deal as at-risk, and shows it on a dashboard. Then it waits for a human to open the dashboard, notice the flag, decide what to do, and do it. Most of the time — managers spend less than 5% of their time coaching, and reps spend less than 40% of their week selling — nothing happens. The dashboard is a report. The report assumes someone will act on it. In practice, the report is the ceiling of what the tool does, not the floor. What the next generation of deal insights looks like The shift is from what happened to what to do about it, and did anyone do it . Three things drive that shift: Deal risk surfaces where the rep works. In the CRM, in the calendar, in the follow-up drafting queue — not on a separate dashboard the rep visits once a quarter. The action is drafted, not recommended. A follow-up email drafted and waiting for review. A CRM field pre-filled and waiting for approval. A next-step suggestion in the deal record with the reasoning attached. The dashboard is a byproduct of adoption, not the reason for it. If reps use the tool because it saves them 30 minutes per call and drafts their follow-ups, the leadership visibility comes for free. If the tool exists only for the leader, no one uses it and the data goes stale within a quarter. One Demodesk customer put it directly in a recent quarterly review: “I like the rep actions part of it. That's good. That's a good addition.” The dashboard wasn't the thing that landed. The actions taken on the rep's behalf were. How Demodesk approaches deal insights Demodesk records every sales conversation — video, phone, in-person via mobile app — and acts on the record. AI Deal Insights flags deal risk from what was said on the call, not from CRM stage guesses. AI CRM Concierge drafts field updates and follow-ups with 99% accuracy and waits for the rep to approve before pushing. AI Coach scores the call against your methodology in seconds so the coaching conversation is grounded in the specific call, not a monthly dashboard review. The dashboard exists — AI Analyst answers any question across your sales data on demand — but it's not the hero. The rep actions are. That's the wedge: Demodesk is built for the rep, not the dashboard . Leadership visibility is the byproduct of a tool reps use, not the reason the tool exists. For a European sales team weighing conversation intelligence platforms, this changes the buying question. Not “which dashboard is prettiest.” Which tool will your reps still be using in six months, and what does it do for them between the recording and the report? Why dashboards fail in mid-market sales Mid-market sales teams (100 to 5,000 employees) are structurally different from enterprise. The team is small enough that the VP knows every rep and every large deal by name. A dashboard that tells the VP something they already know — Sarah's champion went quiet on the Enpal deal — trains the VP to stop opening the tool. What works instead: the tool notices the champion went quiet, drafts a re-engagement email in Sarah's voice, and puts it in her drafts folder with the context of the last three calls attached. Sarah reviews it, edits, sends. The VP finds out when the deal closes, not when it slips. This is the operational shift conversation intelligence is going through in 2026. The $2.9B revenue intelligence category grew on the promise of visibility. The next layer — the AI sales platform — grows on the promise of action. Visibility is table stakes. Action is the wedge.

title: EV Charging Trends in the U.S. for 2026: Convenience, Confidence & Control
summary: Discover the latest EV charging trends in the U.S. for 2026. Explore shifts in home charging, nationwide fast-charging networks, and energy management solutions.
body_text: EV Charging Trends in the U.S. for 2026: Convenience, Confidence & Control 4 min read Electric vehicles in the U.S. are entering a new phase, one defined by scale. As 2026 begins, millions of American drivers are discovering that EV ownership isn’t about radical change. It’s about convenience , especially at home. Here’s what’s predicted to shape EV charging across the U.S. this year. Level 2 Home Charging Is the Backbone of EV Life in America In the U.S., EV charging starts at home – and in 2026, Level 2 AC charging will be the norm. Most drivers: Charge overnight, taking advantage of cheaper electricity rates Wake up to a full battery, driving on electricity generated while they sleep Rarely rely on public charging day-to-day Wallbox’s Pulsar Plus reflects this reality. Offering up to 11.5 kW of charging, compatibility with J1772 and NACS connectors, and smart scheduling through the top-rated Wallbox app , it fits seamlessly into American homes. No matter your setup, home charging is simply the most affordable way to drive electric. Faster, Simpler Public Charging Expands Nationwide Public charging in the U.S. is growing fast, with a strong focus on DC fast charging . 2026 trends are likely to include: More fast chargers along highways Higher reliability standards Simplified payment and Plug & Charge experiences Solutions like Wallbox Supernova are designed for this environment, supporting high utilisation, modular servicing, and consistent performance. For drivers, fast public charging is becoming a predictable part of road trips, rather than a gamble. Apartments, Workplaces, and Fleets Catch Up As EV ownership spreads beyond single-family homes, shared charging is gaining traction. Workplaces, apartments, and fleets increasingly rely on: Load-managed AC charging User authentication Scalable infrastructure Wallbox’s Pulsar Pro charger supports these environments, enabling dozens of vehicles to charge efficiently without costly grid upgrades. Range Anxiety Is No Longer the Barrier Modern EVs routinely exceed 300 miles of range. Combined with expanding fast-charging networks, range anxiety continues to fade. In 2026, we’ll see drivers: Plan routes digitally Trust charger availability Spend less time thinking about range altogether EV ownership is becoming about freedom , as opposed to limitation. Charging Meets Energy Management EVs are increasingly part of broader energy conversations in the U.S. – especially where solar, time-of-use pricing, and incentives are involved. Smart charging allows drivers to: Charge when electricity is cheapest Reduce peak demand and strain on the grid Align driving with cleaner energy Wallbox’s connected ecosystem supports this shift, helping drivers turn charging into an advantage instead of an expense. Check out our EVSE Incentives Search Tool , to quickly identify local, state, and utility rebates available for home charging installations across the U.S. 🔍 Wallbox EVSE Incentives tool Bidirectional Charging Turns EVs into Home Energy Assets One of the most important shifts arriving in the U.S. in 2026 goes beyond charging altogether: bidirectional energy flow . As more American homes adopt solar panels, home batteries, and time-based electricity pricing, EVs are increasingly becoming part of the home’s energy system, not just a vehicle parked in the garage. Bidirectional charging allows drivers to use the energy stored in their EV to power their home, support renewable self-consumption, or provide backup during outages. This is where solutions like Wallbox Quasar 2 come into play. Designed for seamless integration with solar, batteries, and existing home setups, bidirectional charging enables drivers to: Power their home using their EV during peak energy hours Store surplus solar energy and use it when electricity is most expensive Keep essential appliances running during power outages (for up to three days!) Reduce or even eliminate the need for costly stationary home batteries In a country where grid resilience, extreme weather, and energy costs are growing concerns, bidirectional charging adds a new layer of confidence. Your EV becomes a flexible energy resource you control. With EV adoption maturing in the U.S., bidirectional charging represents the next evolution of ownership: mobility that works for your home. Final Thought: EVs in the U.S. Are About Ease The biggest EV trend in America for 2026 isn’t speed or range – it’s simplicity . Charge at home. Charge fast when needed. Let smart technology handle the rest. Owning an EV no longer requires compromise, and that’s when adoption truly accelerates. title: Lyra Schramm joins Intapp as Chief People and Places Officer

body_text: Palo Alto, Calif. — July 13, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the leading governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announces Lyra Schramm has joined the company as Chief People and Places Officer. “We are thrilled to welcome Lyra to the Intapp leadership team,” said John Hall, CEO of Intapp. “As we continue to scale and advance our AI platform for professional firms, Lyra’s leadership will be instrumental in attracting, developing, and retaining the talent required to deliver on that mission.” Schramm is a global Chief People Officer and human capital strategist who partners with founders, CEOs, and boards to scale technology companies through moments of hypergrowth, disruption, and transformation. title: 'A Day Like No Other', the Series That Chronicles Raphael's Life, Arrives on Netflix 9 October
summary: Netflix has announced the release date, the first images and the teaser poster for 'A Day Like No Other'
body_text: Entertainment 23 July 2026 Global Spain Link copied to clipboard DOWNLOAD THE IMAGES DOWNLOAD THE TEASER POSTER Netflix has today announced the release date, the first images and the teaser poster for A Day Like no Other , the biographical series based on the life of the renowned Spanish singer Raphael, which will premiere exclusively on Netflix in Spain and Latin America on 9 October . Javier Morgade ( Culpa tuya , El jardinero ) and Carlos Santos ( El refugio atómico , 1992 ) portray Raphael at two stages of his life – his youth and his maturity, respectively – in a story that explores the highs and lows of the artist’s life. The cast is rounded off by Francesco Carril ( Los años nuevos , La virgen de agosto ), Natalia Varela ( Ella es tu padre , No te puedes esconder ), Pepa Aniorte ( Sueños de libertad , La caza. Guadiana ) and Manolo Caro ( Entrevías , Feria: la luz más oscura ), amongst others. A Day Like no Other is an eight-episode biographical series that recounts the life of Raphael, from his humble beginnings in post-war Spain to his conquest of the world’s greatest stages. The series portrays the unstoppable rise of a one-of-a-kind artist: his most intimate passions, his greatest hits, his personal struggles and the demons that have haunted him throughout his life. Set against backdrops ranging from Madrid to Las Vegas, via Moscow, Paris and Acapulco, A Day Like no Other is an emotional journey through five decades full of highs and lows. A moving story that reveals the man behind the legend. The series is produced by DLO Producciones ( El jardinero , Ni una más ) in association with Caracol Televisión . It is directed by Tito López Amado , Javier Pulido and Beatriz Sanchís , with J osé Manuel Lorenzo as producer and Jacobo Martos as associate producer. The screenplay was written by Ignacio del Moral , Paloma Rando and Adrià P. Xancó . The executive producers are Nacho Bolonio , Dago García , Gonzalo Cordoba , Asier Aguilar , Lisette Osorio and José Manuel Lorenzo About DLO Producciones José Manuel Lorenzo, founder, chairman and executive producer of DLO, established this fiction, film and television production company in 2011; the Banijay Group has held a stake in the company since 2013. DLO comprises a multidisciplinary team of audiovisual professionals with extensive experience and a track record of successful projects: Anatomía de un instante (Movistar Plus+), directed by Alberto Rodríguez and winner of the FORQUÉ Award for Best Series. The La caza trilogy for RTVE ( Monteperdido , Tramuntana and Guadiana ), which made the leap to Movistar Plus+ with LA CAZA. IRATI ; Dime Quién Soy (Movistar Plus+); El Inmortal (Movistar Plus+, Telemundo), nominated at the 2022 Cannes Film Festival and already spanning three series; Ni una más , the adaptation of Miguel Sáez Carral’s novel for Netflix; Las largas sombras , directed by Clara Roquet, for Disney+; El Jardinero , created by Miguel Sáez Carral for Netflix; and his most recent production for the same platform: La acusación . About Caracol Televisión Caracol Televisión is Colombia’s leading television channel for Spanish-language content, having produced several of the industry’s most successful and innovative programmes and formats over the last 20 years. With over 1,900 hours of content produced annually and extensive international sales experience spanning more than 180 countries across five continents, Caracol Televisión is a global pioneer. Today, it is a veritable content production powerhouse, having expanded its influence worldwide through its international business division. With offices in Miami, Madrid and Bogotá, Caracol Internacional distributes the telenovelas, series and entertainment formats created by Caracol TV, which have transcended all cultural and linguistic barriers to become globally recognised products. title: Vertiv Cooling Systems for Edge Computing Now Available with Industrys First IoT Mobile App for Cooling Monitoring and Management
summary: Vertiv™, formerly Emerson Network Power, announces that two of its most popular Liebert® cooling systems for small IT spaces are now available with the iCOMTM CMS Monitoring and Control System that enables remote monitoring, management and alarm troubleshooting for IT managers and service technicians.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio – (January 26, 2017) – Vertiv™, formerly Emerson Network Power, announces that two of its most popular Liebert® cooling systems for small IT spaces are now available with the iCOMTM CMS Monitoring and Control System that enables remote monitoring, management and alarm troubleshooting for IT managers and service technicians. iCOM CMS is now available in North America for the Liebert SRCTM Mini-Split Cooling System and Liebert Mini-Mate2 Ceiling Mounted Precision Cooling System. iCOM CMS provides enhanced protection, visibility and control for small IT spaces that are increasingly used for edge computing and have become critical links to the cloud. iCOM CMS operates through the industry’s first Internet of Things (IoT) mobile app, the web or building management systems (BMS), allowing IT managers to view room and equipment conditions and alarm notifications, remotely manage cooling systems, and track the progress of troubleshooting and repair through automated workflow tracking. The Liebert SRC is a high efficiency, easy-to-install mini-split air conditioning system that provides cooling for server rooms, network closets and other small IT spaces. Offering 4.5kW-9kW cooling capacity, the Liebert SRC provides simple building management system connectivity and is less expensive and faster to deploy than ducted systems. The Liebert Mini-Mate2 is a zero-footprint computer room cooling system for 7x24 temperature and humidity control. Offering 3.5-28kW cooling capacity, it installs above a dropped ceiling. Monitoring and remote management are among the top three concerns facing North American IT professionals regarding the management of small IT spaces, according to the Vertiv “2016 Cooling the Edge Survey.” Nearly half of the survey’s respondents said that these small spaces are mission critical, as they contribute to company revenues. “The availability of iCOM CMS with our new mini-split and ceiling mounted systems is a big advantage for IT managers struggling with the challenges of protecting and monitoring remote spaces, and responding quickly when issues arise,” said John Peter (JP) Valiulis, vice president, North America thermal management marketing, Vertiv. “It provides reliable, cost-effective management of these revenue-critical spaces and combines high efficiency cooling with the ability to monitor and manage these spaces from virtually anywhere.” To learn more about Vertiv cooling solutions for small IT spaces, visit VertivCo.com . About Vertiv Vertiv designs, builds and services critical infrastructure that enables vital applications for data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial facilities. Formerly Emerson Network Power, Vertiv supports today’s growing mobile and cloud computing markets with a portfolio of power, thermal and infrastructure management solutions including the ASCO®, Chloride®, Liebert®, NetSure™ and Trellis™ brands. Sales in fiscal 2016 were $4.4 billion. For more information, visit VertivCo.com . Media Contact: Allen Pfenninger, Fahlgren Mortine (for Vertiv) 216-298-4653 allen.pfenninger@Fahlgren.com

title: WeRide | WeRide and Renault Group Return to Roland-Garros for Third Straight Year with Autonomous Robobus Service
summary: WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) is a leading global commercial-stage company that develops autonomous driving technologies from Level 2 to Level 4.
body_text: PARIS, France – May 26, 2026 – WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD, HKEX: 0800), a global leader in autonomous driving technology, today announced that it will once again deploy its autonomous Robobus at the Roland-Garros tournament – marking the third consecutive year of operations in partnership with Renault Group. Since 2024, the WeRide Robobus has provided the only autonomous public shuttle service at Roland-Garros, showcasing next-generation autonomous driving technology at one of the world's most prestigious sporting events. WeRide Robobus at Roland-Garros Held annually in Paris, Roland-Garros – also known as the French Open – is one of the four Grand Slam tennis tournaments, drawing top-ranked players and hundreds of thousands of spectators each year. Its high‑density, high‑demand transport environment offers a real‑world stage to demonstrate the maturity and reliability of WeRide’s autonomous driving technology. This year, beti serves as the vehicle operator, overseeing daily on-ground operations. During the event, the Robobus will operate along a 2.8‑kilometer route with a journey time of 12 minutes, connecting three stops – Carrefour des Anciens Combattants, Gate 5 Village Welcome Desk, and Porte d’Auteuil – along Avenue de la Porte d'Auteuil, which runs through the Roland-Garros stadium complex. WeRide Robobus runs through the Roland-Garros stadium complex along a 2.8‑kilometer route at Roland-Garros, connecting three stops The service runs from May 24 to June 7 , operating daily from 10.30am to 5pm, 6pm to 8pm, and 10pm to midnight. It also marks the second consecutive year of night‑time operations at Roland‑Garros, extending service hours following a successful rollout in 2025. This builds on WeRide and Renault Group's broader collaboration across Europe, including the launch of a fully driverless Robobus service in France’s Drôme region in March 2025, and a pilot service in central Barcelona the same month – marking Spain’s first public‑road trial of a L4 autonomous vehicle for passenger transport. Europe is a key market in WeRide’s global expansion strategy, with active deployments across France, Belgium, Switzerland, and Slovakia . Beyond France and Spain, WeRide’s Robobus is now in regular commercial operation in Belgium and has removed the front‑row safety driver from its Robobus at Zurich Airport, marking a key step towards fully driverless operations. In parallel, driverless Robotaxi services are set to launch in Furttal, Switzerland, while WeRide has also recently announced its entry into Slovakia as part of Europe’s first large-scale, multi-product autonomous driving commercial deployment. Together, these developments reinforce the company's accelerating expansion and its commitment to scaling autonomous mobility solutions across the region. About WeRide WeRide is a global leader and a first mover in the autonomous driving industry, as well as the first publicly traded Robotaxi company. Our autonomous vehicles have been tested or operated in over 40 cities across 12 countries. We are also the first and only technology company whose products have received autonomous driving permits in eight markets: China, the UAE, Singapore, France, Switzerland, Saudi Arabia, Belgium, and the US. Empowered by the smart, versatile, cost-effective, and highly adaptable WeRide One platform, WeRide provides autonomous driving products and services from L2 to L4, addressing transportation needs in the mobility, logistics, and sanitation industries. WeRide was named to Fortune's 2025 Change the World and 2025 Future 50 lists. https://www.weride.ai About Renault Renault Group is at the forefront of a mobility that is reinventing itself. The Group relies on the complementarity of its three automotive brands – Renault, Dacia, Alpine – and its financial captive – Mobilize Financial Services – to offer sustainable and innovative mobility solutions to its customers. Established in more than 100 countries, Renault Group sold 2.337 million vehicles in 2025. It employs more than 100,000 people who embody its Purpose every day, so that mobility brings people closer. Ready to pursue challenges both on the road and in competition, the Group is committed to an ambitious and value-generating transformation focused on the development of new technologies and services, and a new range of even more competitive, balanced, and electrified vehicles. In line with environmental challenges, Renault Group's ambition is to achieve carbon neutrality in Europe by 2040 and worldwide by 2050. More information: http://www.renaultgroup.com/en About beti beti provides digital services and solutions to clients, mobility operators, and automated driving technology providers in Europe, supporting the large-scale deployment of automated shuttles and robotaxis. beti has been collaborating with WeRide in Europe since October 2024. Macif, the leading insurance group in France, is a shareholder of beti and contributes to the growth of these new mobility solutions in Europe. title: The Sher sisters share a charge in the energy industry
summary: Separated by miles but united by purpose, sisters Lauren and Rebecca Sher are building meaningful careers at NextEra Energy Resources while inspiring each other every step of the way.
body_text: JUNO BEACH, Fla. – From a small coastal town in Texas to shaping the future of energy across the country, sisters Lauren and Rebecca Sher have taken different paths and yet arrived at a shared purpose. Growing up in Bay City, Texas, the Sher sisters spent most of their time outdoors—fishing with their dad, playing sports and learning early lessons about discipline and hard work. Those early experiences, along with strong role models at home, helped shape careers rooted in curiosity, resilience and a drive to contribute to something bigger than themselves. Lauren’s path led her to Tulane University. When Hurricane Katrina forced campus closures, she temporarily relocated to the University of Texas before ultimately launching a career in Washington, D.C., where she worked on Capitol Hill focusing on energy, environmental and agricultural policy. “Energy went from interesting to essential,” Lauren says. “You realize the decisions being made have real consequences—for communities, for reliability, for the future.” Her work brought her into close collaboration with industry leaders, including teams at NextEra Energy Resources, where she helped navigate environmental policy. “When the chance came to join NextEra Energy Resources, it felt like a natural next step,” Lauren says. “It was a place where I could take everything I’d learned and apply it in a tangible way.” Today, Lauren works in Origination, partnering with public power entities, municipalities and cooperatives to help meet their energy needs. Rebecca’s journey took a different route. After studying political science and environmental science at Wellesley College, she spent summers working in national parks—an experience that helped define her future. “That experience changed everything,” she says. “It’s when I knew I wanted to build a life connected to the outdoors and in the Western U.S.” She went on to law school at the University of Colorado with plans to pursue environmental law, but a course in Tribal jurisdiction shifted her trajectory. “I was completely hooked,” Rebecca says. “It’s meaningful work, and it matters deeply to communities.” She built her early career representing Tribal nations before an unexpected conversation with her sister opened a new door. While Lauren was working in Washington, she connected Rebecca with a colleague at NextEra Energy Resources. Not long after, Rebecca joined the company. “I had built a career I loved,” Rebecca says. “But I saw how happy Lauren was and how much opportunity there was to grow. I decided to try something new—and it paid off.” Now in a development role, Rebecca helps bring energy solutions to life, working at the intersection of projects and the communities they serve. Despite living on opposite sides of the country—Lauren in Florida and Rebecca in Colorado—the sisters remain closely connected. They talk often and support each other through career and personal milestones. “My sister is my role model,” Rebecca says. “She’s always been my champion.” Their bond goes back to childhood. Just 17 months apart, they were often mistaken for twins. They played the same sports, waking up before sunrise for swim practice and learning early how to balance school, athletics and jobs. “We had to figure out how to prioritize and work hard,” Rebecca says. “That’s stayed with us.” Today, both are raising young families—Lauren with two children and Rebecca with three. Though they now live across the country from one another, their work and family continue to intersect in meaningful ways. “We’ve both just kept saying yes,” Rebecca says. That mindset, combined with a shared commitment to service, continues to guide the m in careers at NextEra Energy Resources. Their paths may look different, but at the core, they are driven by the same values instilled years ago .

title: Introducing API Version 2026-03-30
summary: We're excited to announce API version 2026-03-30 — introducing redesigned Attributes for Entities and Accounts.
body_text: We’re excited to announce the release of API version 2026-03-30 , featuring redesigned Attributes for both Entities and Accounts . This release expands the attributes product with richer computed outputs, a unified per-attribute result shape, and support for asynchronous attribute computation workflows. ​ What’s New ​ Entity Attributes The Entity Attributes API now returns a broader set of aggregated financial attributes computed across an Entity’s connected accounts. These attributes are organized across categories such as revolving credit cards, personal loans, mortgages, installment balances, and overall utilization. Key improvements: Introduces a richer set of financial attributes, including balances, utilization trends, deltas, delinquency signals, and payment behavior metrics Returns attributes in a simplified { value, error } shape — error uses the standard { type, sub_type, code, message } format when the attribute could not be computed Computes all supported entity attributes automatically as part of the request lifecycle Supports asynchronous processing so teams can poll or rely on webhook-driven workflows for completion Available when passing Method-Version: 2026-03-30 in the request header. Example Response { "id" : "attr_dADraNgLBrhgL" , "entity_id" : "ent_EQ3FCTzDUmmCb" , "status" : "completed" , "attributes" : { "revolving_credit_card_balance_total" : { "value" : 968400 , "error" : null }, "credit_limit_total" : { "value" : 8100000 , "error" : null }, "credit_card_utilization" : { "value" : 11.96 , "error" : null }, "overall_utilization" : { "value" : 70.5 , "error" : null } }, "error" : null , "created_at" : "2026-04-09T17:02:47.910Z" , "updated_at" : "2026-04-09T17:04:35.220Z" } ​ Account Attributes The Account Attributes API has been expanded into a dedicated account-level attributes product. Returned attributes now vary by liability type, including support for credit cards, personal loans, and mortgages. Key improvements: Adds account-level financial attributes such as utilization trends, delinquency flags, and installment estimates Returns attributes in a simplified { value, error } shape with standardized error objects Supports asynchronous attribute computation workflows for account requests Adds webhook support for account attribute lifecycle events Available when passing Method-Version: 2026-03-30 in the request header. Example Response { "id" : "acc_attr_cWBKqwVP87kim" , "account_id" : "acc_4m9amk4KFiaQX" , "status" : "completed" , "attributes" : { "type" : { "value" : "credit_card" , "error" : null }, "usage_pattern" : { "value" : "revolver" , "error" : null }, "delinquency_flag" : { "value" : false , "error" : null }, "utilization" : { "value" : 11.96 , "error" : null } }, "error" : null , "created_at" : "2026-04-09T17:02:47.910Z" , "updated_at" : "2026-04-09T17:04:35.220Z" } ​ Account Attribute Subscriptions Accounts can now be enrolled in an attribute Subscription for continuous monitoring of an Account’s financial attributes. Once enrolled, Method automatically computes new Account Attributes and notifies your team via webhooks as they change. curl https://production.methodfi.com/accounts/{acc_id}/subscriptions \ -X POST \ -H "Method-Version: 2026-03-30" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_WyZEWVfTcH7GqmPzUPk65Vjc" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "enroll": "attribute" }' Available for credit card, personal loan, and mortgage accounts The attribute subscription appears in an Account’s available_subscriptions once eligible Available when passing Method-Version: 2026-03-30 in the request header. ​ New Webhook Events This version adds webhook coverage for the new account attribute resource lifecycle. New events: entity_attribute.create entity_attribute.update account_attribute.create account_attribute.update See Webhooks for the complete event list. ​ Breaking Changes Entity Attributes request semantics changed POST /entities/{ent_id}/attributes now computes all supported attributes automatically The legacy request body for selecting specific credit_health_* attributes is no longer documented for 2026-03-30 Entity Attributes response shape changed Legacy attribute payloads that returned value and rating have been replaced with a simplified { value, error } shape On success, error is null . On failure, error contains a standard { type, sub_type, code, message } object (e.g. ENTITY_ATTRIBUTE_INSUFFICIENT_DATA code 27001 for entity attributes, ACCOUNT_ATTRIBUTE_INSUFFICIENT_DATA code 28001 for account attributes) Attribute names now reflect the new attribute model Account Attributes response shape changed Account attribute responses now use the same simplified { value, error } result structure Attribute availability now depends on the account’s liability type Attributes create endpoints are asynchronous Create requests now return an in-progress resource that must be polled or observed via webhook until completion ​ Why It Matters This release makes the attributes product more useful for underwriting, servicing, monitoring, and decisioning workflows. With this release, developers can: Retrieve a richer set of entity- and account-level financial signals Build against a consistent result format across attributes Handle unavailable computations explicitly using standardized error objects with type , sub_type , code , and message Use asynchronous workflows that better fit long-running computations ​ Upgrading to 2026-03-30 The new API version is available to all existing teams. New teams are automatically pinned to 2026-03-30 . Request Header: Set Method-Version to 2026-03-30 . See API Versioning for more information. Client Libraries: Check your Method SDK version and upgrade guidance before moving production traffic to the new API version. Once upgraded, rollbacks to prior API versions are not supported. Contact your Method CSM for upgrade assistance. ​ Upgrade Support Our technical integration team is available to help review your current usage of Attributes and plan a migration to 2026-03-30 . Contact your Method CSM for upgrade support.
